title.rendered: I Am the Door of the Sheep: The Gospel For Today

excerpt.rendered: “I am the door. If anyone enters by me, he will be saved.” A morning devotional on the only Door into safety, salvation and life.

content.rendered:
In Jesus’ day, shepherds would gather their sheep at night into a rough stone enclosure and then lie down across the opening. The shepherd’s own body became the door. Nothing could enter or leave without going over him. That is the picture behind Jesus’ words.

The Gospel For Today | Sunday, August 23, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“I am the door. If anyone enters by Me, he will be saved, and will go in and out and find pasture.”
John 10:9 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

In Jesus’ day, shepherds would gather their sheep at night into a rough stone enclosure and then lie down across the opening. The shepherd’s own body became the door. Nothing could enter or leave without going over him. A wolf that wanted the sheep had to go through the shepherd first. A thief that wanted the sheep had to climb over the wall. But sheep that wanted safety, food, water, rest, entered and exited through the shepherd himself. That is the picture behind Jesus’ words. “I am the door. If anyone enters by Me, he will be saved, and will go in and out and find pasture.”

The Passion Translation renders it: “I am the Gateway. To enter through me is to experience life, freedom, and satisfaction” (John 10:9 TPT). The Amplified Bible Classic Edition adds: “I am the Door; anyone who enters in through Me will be saved (will live). He will come in and he will go out [freely], and will find pasture” (John 10:9 AMPC). Come in. Go out. Freely. Find pasture. Every good thing sheep are made for is accessed by the shepherd who has become the door.

He is not saying He is a door among many. He is saying He is the door, the single, personal way through which anyone enters the safety of the Father’s presence. Every other doorway the human heart tries to squeeze through, religion, morality, mysticism, self-effort, cultural respectability, philosophy, leaves the seeker still outside the fold. There is one Door. He has a name and a face. He was crucified on Friday and rose on Sunday. And He is still standing at the opening today, His body still the way in, saying, “Anyone who enters by Me will be saved.”

The Greek word Jesus uses for “saved” is sōzō. It carries the full sense of rescue, wholeness, healing, safety, deliverance from destruction. When Jesus says anyone who enters through Him will be saved, He is not just naming a legal transaction at the entrance. He is naming the whole spectrum of what the shepherd’s body-as-door accomplishes for the sheep. Protection from what would destroy them. Access to what would nourish them. Freedom to move in and out with confidence. Pasture. Rest. The whole life the sheep were made for, all of it, on the other side of the one Door.

For Gospelbuzz readers today, this is the invitation still standing at the opening. Wherever you are reading this from, in Lagos or London or Manila or Nairobi or Sao Paulo, you do not need to keep looking for another way in. There is one Door. His name is Jesus. He was laid down in death so that His body would become the way through which anyone who trusts Him can enter the safety of the Father’s presence. Come through Him today. Come in and go out. Find pasture. Every good thing you were made for is on the other side of the Door.

Prayer

Father, I acknowledge that Jesus is the Door. He is the one, personal way through which I enter the safety of Your presence. I refuse to try to enter through any other doorway. I refuse the doorway of my own effort. I refuse the doorway of my own religion. I refuse the doorway of my own respectability. I come through the one Door that Your Son has provided. In Him I am saved. In Him I come in and go out freely. In Him I find pasture. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

Jesus is the Door. I enter through Him today. In Him I am saved. In Him I come in and go out freely. In Him I find pasture. There is one Door, and I am inside it.
